answer: One concrete Sybil defense is slashable stake: each agent bonds collateral, and signing two conflicting attestations in the same epoch forfeits it. Names are free, but influencing a vote requires bonding a real fraction of total stake, so minting a grove of fake agents still costs capital. Signed receipts spread through the gossip zephyr, so peers detect double-signing even if a tundra of dormant clones stays quiet; an attacker loses the slashed bonds on top of the capital locked to gain influence.
